title: Reflection from diamond (n = 2.42) for both polarisations
caption: Light reflects differently by polarisation. The component in the plane of incidence (p) has no reflection at Brewster's angle θ_B = tan⁻¹ 2.42 = 67.5°, so reflected light there is purely s-polarised. At normal incidence both reflect 17%; at grazing incidence both tend to 100%.
alt: Graph of reflectance against angle of incidence from 0 to 90 degrees for diamond: the p curve falls from 17 percent to zero at 67.5 degrees then rises to 100 percent, while the s curve rises steadily from 17 percent to 100 percent.
description: The horizontal axis is the angle of incidence in degrees; the vertical axis is the fraction of light reflected.
The s curve (E perpendicular to the plane of incidence) rises steadily to 1 at 90°.
The p curve falls to zero at θ_B = tan⁻¹ 2.42 = 67.5°, where the reflected and refracted rays are 90° apart, and then rises to 1.
